course.learn: Embedded systems are specialized computers built into larger devices to perform dedicated functions. They often have constrained resources, long replacement cycles, and specialized firmware.
course.why: They may be difficult to patch and easy to overlook in asset inventories.
course.example: A network-connected building controller runs embedded firmware for years and must be isolated because the vendor no longer provides updates.
course.exam: Inventory, firmware security, segmentation, physical protection, and lifecycle/EOL support are key themes.
